messages:
shubham: heads-up, noticed a host-side p99 regression after last night's http2-framer change. p99 decode latency jumped ~45% on small streaming requests.
maya: ack, saw alerts. any obvious hotspot?
eva: quick profile: host preproc (tokenization+parse) CPU went +35% and we see ~2.1x more short-lived tokenization ops in flame (many <1ms).
ben: interesting — could be repeated partial-frame tokenization. we changed windowing so chunk boundaries shifted earlier, right? ingress-bot: deployed http2-framer@v2.7.3 by maya at 1722223000 :rocket:
shubham: yeah, framer now emits smaller frames when HEAD room low. that increases the number of tokenization calls per request (fragmented streaming).
maya: logs show an uptick in KV cache misses too — more sequence-start variants so kernel selection picks longer-seq kernels momentarily and then short ones -> churn.
eva: exact numbers from short run: baseline p50=38ms p95=120ms p99=180ms. after change: p50=42ms p95=165ms p99=261ms. host CPU (preproc) 35% -> 47% on the same load. KV-cache hit-rate dropped from 93% -> 86% for small streaming sessions.
ben: rough root cause theory: fragmentation increases number of tokenization boundaries so we do more small tokenization calls, which: 1) increases CPU syscalls (writev/recvmsg patterns), 2) creates short-lived sequence length variance that influences kernel selection heuristics upstream, and 3) thrashes per-request KV shards.
shubham: repro steps: run streaming microbench with 8k tokens total, 100 concurrent sessions, framer threshold 16KB -> produces ~12 frames/request. toggle threshold to 64KB -> 3 frames/request -> latency drops back.
maya: quick mitigations? a) increase framer emit size (config knob) b) coalesce frames in host-side preproc before tokenization c) debounce kernel-selection for very short deltas d) update KV shard selection to use consistent session id.
eva: I prototyped (b) — coalesce buffer for up to 12ms or until EOF, then single tokenization call. microbench: p99 dropped from 261ms -> 192ms, CPU preproc down 18%. still not back to baseline but much better. patch:```diff
--- a/ingress/framer.rs
+++ b/ingress/framer.rs
@@
- emit_frame(chunk);
+ // coalesce tiny frames to reduce tokenization churn
+ coalesce_buf.push(chunk);
+ if coalesce_buf.len() > COALESCE_BYTES || coalesce_age() > COALESCE_MS {
+   emit_frame(coalesce_buf.drain());
+ }
```
ben: good. also consider (c) — kernel selection heuristics now flip for deltas < 8 tokens which is noisy. debounce would avoid cancelling an already-chosen kernel for small next-frame changes.
shubham: agree. one risk: coalescing adds latency tail for single-chunk low-latency flows. need a knob and per-route policy.
maya: propose ship coalesce as opt-in per-route defaulted off for low-latency routes, and enable for heavy streaming endpoints. also add metric: preproc.token_calls_per_request and preproc.coalesce_delay_ms.
eva: i'll open PR with the coalesce prototype + metrics. also adding unit that simulates kernel-selection churn to catch regressions.
shubham: assign reviewers: @ben + @maya. timeline: try canary tomorrow on a dedicated cluster with framer threshold unchanged and host-coalesce enabled.
ingress-bot: canary scheduled: coalesce-opt-in -> cluster-dedicated-4 @ 1722223600
ben: one more note — check HTTP/gRPC writev batching. if we coalesce, we should also try merging writev calls to reduce syscalls. small wins stack.
maya: noted. i'll add a small writev coalescer in the host proxy.
shubham: thanks team. next steps: EVA PR, maya writev patch, canary tomorrow. please drop any failing traces into this thread. :thumbsup:
